chunks: The esteemed Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, may God be pleased with him, said: My father, may God have mercy on him, narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid, from Abu al-Jarud, Ibn Bukayr, and Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-'Ijli, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, peace be upon him, who said:

Al-Husayn ibn Ali, peace be upon them both, was killed, and there were found on him three hundred and twenty-something wounds from spears, sword slashes, or arrows. It is reported that they were all on his front side, because he, peace be upon him, would not turn his back.

key_terms.أُصِيبَ: Was killed/struck — a passive verb indicating that Imam al-Husayn was martyred
key_terms.ضَرْبَةً بِسَيْفٍ: A slash from a sword — sword wounds inflicted in close combat
key_terms.طَعْنَةً بِرُمْحٍ: A wound from a spear — one of the three types of wounds found on his body
key_terms.لَا يُوَلِّي: Did not turn his back — a testament to his extraordinary courage and steadfastness
key_terms.مُقَدَّمِهِ: His front side — indicating that he always faced the enemy and never fled

ai.seo_question: How many wounds did Imam Husayn have at Karbala according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) narrated that Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali (AS) was martyred at Karbala bearing over three hundred and twenty wounds inflicted by spears, swords, and arrows. It is reported that all these wounds were found on the front of his body, because he (AS) never turned his back to the enemy.
